title: Collection, Array, and Index
definition: A collection groups multiple values under access and organization rules; an array is an ordered indexed collection whose JavaScript indices begin at zero and whose length defines the normal upper bound.
purpose: Represent ordered multiple values and reason safely about element positions and bounds.
history: Arrays originate as contiguous indexed structures in many languages; JavaScript arrays are dynamic objects with array-specific length and indexed-property semantics.
mental_model: A numbered row of compartments from zero through length minus one, while recognizing that JavaScript arrays can contain holes and mixed values.
analogy: Numbered seats; useful for order and bounds, but JavaScript arrays are more dynamic than a fixed physical row.
common_mistakes: Using length as last valid index
industry_notes: Collection choice should reflect order, access, uniqueness, and update needs; C17 focuses on ordered arrays.
ai_notes: Require empty, single, multiple, and out-of-bounds cases in AI-generated collection code.
interview_notes: Ask why the last valid index is length minus one.
